Respiratory Illness Outbreak Disrupts Oil & Gas Operations in Kuwait

A sudden outbreak of respiratory illness has affected numerous workers in Kuwait’s Oil & Gas Producers sector, causing operational slowdowns and raising health concerns across several sites. The Ministry of Health confirmed on Thursday that over 180 cases of acute respiratory infection have been reported among staff stationed at the Burgan and West Sabriya fields, as well as at processing and support facilities in the Ahmadi and Mina Abdullah regions.

According to Dr. Faisal Al-Rashidi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Health, “The outbreak is being closely monitored. Most patients are experiencing fever, cough, and shortness of breath. While the source of the illness is under investigation, initial findings indicate a possible viral origin.”

Operations at key extraction and processing sites have been partially curtailed in response to the outbreak, with some facilities, including those run by Gulf Star Petroleum and Kuwaiti Energy Solutions, reportedly reducing shifts to minimize contact between workers. “We have implemented staggered shifts and enhanced sanitization protocols,” said Saad Al-Mutairi, health and safety manager at Kuwaiti Energy Solutions. “However, workforce shortages are already impacting our daily output.”

Industry analysts estimate that production at affected sites has dropped by as much as 15 percent since the outbreak began late last week. “There is concern that an extended disruption could affect export schedules and contract obligations,” said Amal Hasan, an independent energy analyst based in Kuwait City. “The sector is highly interdependent, so even modest reductions in workforce availability have significant consequences.”

The Kuwait Oil & Gas Workers Union has called for urgent measures to protect staff, including expanded medical screening and improved quarantine facilities at worksites. “Our members’ safety must come first,” stated union chair Khaled Al-Majid. “We urge all companies to cooperate fully with health authorities and to prioritize transparency.”

Health teams have been dispatched to the affected sites to conduct testing and deliver medical supplies. The Ministry of Health has not yet determined when the outbreak might be contained, but emphasized that all necessary resources are being mobilized. “We are working round the clock with industry partners,” Dr. Al-Rashidi added. “Our priority is to safeguard workers and restore normal operations as soon as possible.”

The situation remains fluid, and authorities have advised oil and gas companies to remain vigilant and to update contingency plans as the outbreak continues.
